chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Wahb ibn Abd Rabbihi, who said:

I saw Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) picking his teeth, so I looked at him. He said: 'Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to pick his teeth, and he was of the aromatic mouth.'
ai.seo_question: What is the religious significance of using a toothpick in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the Siwak as a confirmed Sunnah by linking the Prophet Muhammad’s practice directly to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, thereby reinforcing the continuity of prophetic tradition in Shia jurisprudence. It underscores the spiritual and physical purity associated with oral hygiene, noting that the Prophet used it specifically to 'perfume the mouth,' which elevates a mundane act of cleanliness to an act of worship and social etiquette.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Wahab Bin Abd Rabbihi who said,

‘I saw Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> picking teeth, so I looked at him<sup>asws</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> used to pick teeth and he<sup>asws</sup> was of the aromatic mouth’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn Mahbub from Wahab ibn ‘Abd Rabbibhi who has said the following:
“I once saw abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, using toothpicks and I looked at him (the Imam). He (the Imam) said, ‘The Messenger of Allah would use a toothpick; it cleanses the mouth.’”
